formation.title: The Unification of Madagascar
formation.text:
The great island stands unified at last. For generations, the Merina of the highlands, the Sakalava of the western coasts, the Betsileo of the southern mountains, and the Antemoro scholars of the southeast each built kingdoms of their own. Now, through conquest, diplomacy, and the sacred authority of hasina, one ruler commands them all.

But unification poses a fundamental question. Madagascar's strength has always been dual: the productive highland rice terraces that feed millions, and the vast coastline whose outrigger fleets connect the island to the trade routes of the Indian Ocean. The new realm must choose which of these traditions will define its character.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We shall cultivate the highlands and rule from the sacred hills.

modifiers.name: Hasina of the Highlands
modifiers.text: The sacred power of the highlands flows through the centralized state. Through irrigation, codified law, and the divine mandate of the andriana, the realm transforms its mountain heartland into the breadbasket of an island nation.

options.text: We shall command the seas from a thousand ports.

modifiers.name: Island of a Thousand Ports
modifiers.text: Madagascar's coasts are alive with outrigger canoes carrying goods across the Mozambique Channel and beyond. Following the Sakalava tradition, the unified island projects power across the Indian Ocean through naval supremacy and merchant fleets.

advances.name: Austronesian Seafaring Heritage
advances.text: The ancestors crossed the Indian Ocean in outrigger canoes. Their descendants maintain this seafaring tradition along Madagascar's coasts.

advances.name: Legacy of the Vazimba
advances.text: The highland warriors who displaced the first inhabitants of Madagascar forged a martial tradition of spear and shield that endures in the Mpiambina companies.

advances.name: Irrigated Rice Paddies
advances.text: The Betsileo technique of terraced, irrigated rice cultivation transforms the highland valleys into the most productive farmland in the Indian Ocean.

advances.name: Zebu Cattle Tradition
advances.text: Zebu cattle are wealth, status, and sacred obligation in Malagasy society. Their horns crown the tombs of the great, their meat feeds the living, and their hides bind the Sorabe manuscripts. The herds are kept in sunken pens beside the villages of the cattle country.

advances.name: Fady Taboo System
advances.text: The elaborate system of fady (ancestral taboos governing behavior, food, places, and time) binds Malagasy society together through shared spiritual obligation.

advances.name: Andriana Caste Order
advances.text: The codification of the andriana noble caste, the hova freemen, and the andevo servile class creates a stable social hierarchy rooted in ancestral status and written decree.

advances.name: Highland Settlement
advances.text: The central highlands offer natural defenses, fertile soil, and freedom from the malaria that plagues the coasts, drawing settlement and population growth.

advances.name: Fokon'olona Village Assemblies
advances.text: The fokon'olona, village councils of elders and notables, govern local affairs through consensus, mediating disputes and organizing communal labor long before any king claimed sovereignty over them.

advances.name: Highland Ironworking
advances.text: The smiths of the highlands smelt iron from laterite ores using charcoal furnaces, producing the tools, weapons, and agricultural implements that sustain the realm.

advances.name: Lamba Silk Weaving
advances.text: The lamba, a woven silk or cotton cloth worn as a shawl by the living and as a shroud for the dead, is the supreme expression of Malagasy textile artistry. The finest lamba akotofahana take months to weave.

advances.name: Sorabe Writing Tradition
advances.text: The Antemoro ombiasy developed the Sorabe script, Malagasy written in Arabic characters, to record astrology, medicine, history, and royal genealogies. They wrote on a paper of their own making, beaten from the bark of the avoha tree.

event.title: The Sorabe Manuscripts
event.text:
The Antemoro scholars of the southeastern coast are the keepers of a remarkable tradition. Descended from Arab and Swahili merchants who settled at the mouth of the Matitanana River, they developed the Sorabe: a system of writing the Malagasy language using Arabic script. Their manuscripts record not only religious texts but also astrological charts, medical remedies, genealogies, and the histories of kings.

Recognizing the power of literacy, the court has invited Antemoro ombiasy to serve as scribes, astrologers, and advisors. For the first time, the laws of the realm and the pronouncements of its rulers will be recorded in writing, bringing order and permanence to what was once transmitted only through oral tradition.

options.text: Let the wisdom of the Sorabe illuminate our court.

modifiers.name: Sorabe Scholarly Tradition
modifiers.text: The Antemoro scholars have brought the art of writing to the court, recording laws, prophecies, and histories in the Arabic-Malagasy Sorabe script.

advances.name: Antemoro Court Astrologers
advances.text: Antemoro ombiasy serve as astrologers and advisors at the courts of Malagasy kings, reading the vintana: the destiny written in the stars and the phases of the moon.

advances.name: Sakalava Expansion
advances.text: The Sakalava kingdoms of Menabe and Boina expand aggressively along the western coast, their warriors moving swiftly through a landscape they know intimately. Wherever Sakalava live, the levy is a warband of spearmen who know that country.

advances.name: Indian Ocean Trade Contacts
advances.text: Arab, Swahili, and later European merchants call at Madagascar's ports, trading cloth, pottery, and metal goods for rice, cattle, beeswax, and enslaved captives.

advances.name: Outrigger War Fleets
advances.text: Sakalava war canoes, large outrigger lakana carrying thirty or more warriors, range across the Mozambique Channel in great seasonal raiding fleets, striking the Comoros and the East African coast.

advances.name: Rova Fortification
advances.text: The hilltop rova complexes (fortified palace-citadels of stone, timber, and hardened clay) combine political residence with military strongpoint, their massive stone disc gates sealed each night.

event.title: The Sacred Hill of Ambohimanga
event.text:
Rising from the central highlands northeast of Antananarivo, the fortified hill of Ambohimanga has become the spiritual heart of the realm. Its rova (a complex of wooden palaces, stone walls, and sacred enclosures) embodies the union of political authority and ancestral power that defines Malagasy rule.

The great gates of Ambohimanga, sealed each night by rolling a massive stone disc across the entrance, guard not merely a settlement but a concept: that the land itself is sacred, and that those who rule from its heights do so with the blessing of the razana: the ancestors who watch over their descendants from the world beyond.

options.text: Ambohimanga shall stand as our eternal citadel.

advances.name: Menabe and Boina Kingdoms
advances.text: The two great Sakalava kingdoms, Menabe in the south and Boina in the north, together dominate western Madagascar and extend their influence across the island.

advances.name: Hasina Sacred Authority
advances.text: Hasina, the sacred power flowing from the ancestors through those who rule, legitimizes their authority and transforms political obedience into spiritual obligation.

advances.name: Indian Ocean Slave Trade
advances.text: The Mascarene plantation economies of Reunion and Mauritius create insatiable demand for enslaved laborers, which Malagasy kingdoms fill for substantial profit.

advances.name: Coastal Raiding Tradition
advances.text: Malagasy raiders in outrigger fleets descend on coastal settlements across the western Indian Ocean, seizing captives and goods in lightning strikes before withdrawing to sea.

advances.name: Trano Gasy Architecture
advances.text: The trano gasy (the traditional Malagasy house of brick, timber, and thatch, oriented north-south according to cosmic principles) evolves into an aristocratic architectural tradition in the highlands.

advances.name: Fanompoana Labor System
advances.text: The fanompoana, corvee labor owed by all free subjects to the state, builds canals, roads, and fortifications, and raises armies. It is the engine of state power and the burden of the common people. Service in the field is counted as part of the labor owed, and the levy is called up with it.

event.title: The Question of Fanompoana
event.text:
The fanompoana, the system of corvee labor owed by all free subjects to the state, has been the engine of the realm's growth. Through fanompoana, irrigation canals have been dug, fortifications raised, roads cut through the jungle, and armies marched to war. Every great work of the state has been built on the backs of its people.

But the system strains under its own weight. Farmers pulled from their fields during planting season return to find their families hungry. Artisans conscripted to distant construction sites cannot ply their trades. The question now confronting the state is whether to intensify fanompoana to fuel greater ambitions, or to commute the obligation into taxes paid in rice and coin, freeing the people to labor for themselves while still filling the state treasury.

options.text: The labor of the people is the foundation of the state.

modifiers.name: Fanompoana State Labor
modifiers.text: The state commands the labor of its subjects for public works, irrigation canals, roads, fortifications, and military service. The state grows powerful, but the cost falls heavy on the common people.

options.text: Let them pay in rice and silver instead.

modifiers.name: Fanompoana Commuted to Taxes
modifiers.text: Rather than demanding labor directly, the state accepts payment in rice and silver. The people prosper in their freed time, and the treasury swells with the fruits of a more efficient economy.

advances.name: Standing Army Reform
advances.text: The state raises permanent regiments, the tafika, armed with a mix of traditional spears and acquired muskets, drilling them into a disciplined standing force.

advances.name: Antananarivo as Capital
advances.text: The city on the thousand hills becomes the undisputed capital of a unified Madagascar, its markets, palaces, and workshops drawing population from across the island.

advances.name: Betsileo Integration
advances.text: The conquered Betsileo kingdoms are integrated into the Merina state, their agricultural expertise, especially terraced rice cultivation, enriching the unified realm.

advances.name: Musket Acquisition and Manufacture
advances.text: Through trade with Europeans and the forced labor of skilled ironworkers, the realm acquires and maintains a growing arsenal of firearms.

advances.name: Mozambique Channel Trade
advances.text: Control of the ports along Madagascar's western coast gives the realm leverage over the trade routes crossing the Mozambique Channel between Africa and the Indian Ocean.

advances.name: Andrianampoinimerina's Reforms
advances.text: The great unifier codifies law, reorganizes the caste system, builds irrigation works, and establishes a centralized administration, transforming a highland chiefdom into a state worthy of the name.

advances.name: Radama's Modernization
advances.text: King Radama embraces European military techniques, inviting British advisors to train his army in musket drill, formation tactics, and disciplined warfare.

event.title: The Modernization of the Realm
event.text:
A new wind blows through the highlands. Inspired by contact with European powers (particularly the British, who have sent military advisors and missionaries), the state undertakes a sweeping program of modernization. Merina soldiers drill in European formations, learning to fire muskets in disciplined volleys rather than the traditional warrior charges.

Beyond the military, the reforms touch every aspect of the realm. A Latin alphabet replaces the Sorabe script for official correspondence. Schools open to teach reading and arithmetic. Artisans are organized into workshops producing goods for the state. The old ways are not abandoned. The fady still govern daily life, and the ancestors still watch from Ambohimanga. But they are joined now by new techniques and new ambitions.

options.text: We shall master the tools of the modern world.

advances.name: British Alliance
advances.text: The Anglo-Merina treaty of 1820 exchanges the abolition of the slave trade for British military assistance, diplomatic recognition, and access to modern technology.

advances.name: Merina Hegemony
advances.text: The highland state extends its authority over two-thirds of Madagascar through military conquest and administrative integration, bringing the coastal peoples under highland control. Soldier-settlers, the voanjo, are planted among the conquered to hold them.

advances.name: Malagasy Literacy Campaign
advances.text: Protestant missionaries and state schools spread literacy across the highlands, replacing the Sorabe script with a Latin alphabet and opening education beyond the Antemoro scholarly caste.

advances.name: Rice Surplus Economy
advances.text: Expanded irrigation and intensive terraced farming produce rice surpluses that fuel population growth, urban specialization, and export trade.

advances.name: Coastal Conquest
advances.text: The Merina navy projects highland power to the coasts, securing ports and trade routes that connect the unified realm to the wider Indian Ocean world.

advances.name: Ranavalona's Defiant Isolation
advances.text: Queen Ranavalona I expels foreign missionaries and traders, seals the realm against European encroachment, and maintains independence through military strength and ruthless self-sufficiency.

advances.name: Malagasy Proto-Industrialization
advances.text: State-organized workshops produce textiles, soap, bricks, and metalwork for domestic consumption, reducing dependence on imported goods.

advances.name: Unified Government of Madagascar
advances.text: A single administrative apparatus governs the entire island, with local governors appointed from the capital replacing the independent kings of old.

advances.name: Port Modernization
advances.text: The realm modernizes its coastal harbors to handle larger vessels and greater trade volumes, connecting Madagascar to global commerce.

advances.name: Malagasy Sovereignty
advances.text: An independent Madagascar, governed by its own laws and traditions, commands respect among the nations of the Indian Ocean.

advances.name: Malagasy Cultural Renaissance
advances.text: The synthesis of highland and coastal, Austronesian and African, traditional and modern traditions creates a distinctive Malagasy cultural identity that transcends the old ethnic divisions.

destiny.name: Destiny of Madagascar
destiny.text: The great island is unified. Now its people must choose how to wield that unity: whether to deepen the roots of the highland state or cast their outrigger sails across the Indian Ocean.

event.title: The Unified Island
event.text: For the first time in living memory, a single authority governs all of Madagascar. From the highland capital to the remotest fishing village on the southern coast, the word of the capital carries the weight of law. The realm has stability. Now it must find purpose.

destiny.name: Highland Consolidation
destiny.text: The rice terraces of the highlands must become the foundation of a prosperous centralized state. Fill the state granaries, raise a town on the hill of Antananarivo, and ensure rice flows through the capital's markets.

conditions.text: We own Antananarivo and it has become a town or a city

children.text: Rice is produced in the market
Rice is traded in the market

event.title: The Granaries of the Highlands
event.text:
The terraced paddies of the central highlands produce rice in abundance that surpasses anything known on this island before. The irrigation canals reach further each year, the hillsides are carved into new fields, and the state granaries overflow with surplus. Antananarivo grows fat on the labor of its people, and the realm's wealth is measured not in gold or silk but in the white grain that feeds millions.

The highland consolidation is complete. The question now is where this agrarian power will be directed.

options.text: The land feeds us. Now we shall shape the world.

destiny.name: Highland Dominion
destiny.text: The realm reaches beyond the island. Seize the gold-rich port of Sofala on the African mainland, terrace the highland valleys for rice in four places, and raise a second highland town at Fianarantsoa to hold the Betsileo country.

conditions.text: We own Fianarantsoa and it has become a town or a city
Own Sofala, or a subject owns it
A Rice Terrace lies in at least 4 of our locations

event.title: Dominion Beyond the Shore
event.text:
Malagasy soldiers stand on foreign soil. The conquest of Sofala brings the realm something it has never had before: access to the gold trade that has enriched the Swahili coast for centuries. The state treasury swells with new revenue, and the realm's influence extends across the Mozambique Channel.

But power abroad demands choices at home. The state must decide how to invest this new wealth.

options.text: Invest in irrigation and the people's welfare.

modifiers.name: State Irrigation Works
modifiers.text: The state invests its new continental revenues into expanding the highland irrigation network, bringing water to terraces that will feed the growing kingdom for generations.

modifiers.name: Highland Fortress Network
modifiers.text: The wealth of Sofala funds a chain of rova fortresses across the highlands, creating an impregnable defensive network that no invader can breach.

destiny.name: The Highland Empire
destiny.text: A continental power rising from an island. Extend control over the Mozambique coast, make Antananarivo a city, give it a library or a printers shop to spread the written word through the realm, and marshal an army that can defend Malagasy sovereignty against any power on earth.

conditions.text: We own Antananarivo and it has become a city
Own Quelimane, or a subject owns it
We own Antananarivo and a Library, Printers Shop, Printing Manufactory or Printing Mill stands there

event.title: Empire of the Highlands
event.text:
The realm that began as a collection of highland villages now commands territory stretching from the interior of Madagascar to the African coast. Malagasy governors administer foreign ports. Malagasy soldiers garrison foreign fortresses. The books of the capital spread literacy to the provinces, binding the realm together with the written word.

This is the apex of Malagasy power. The state must choose how to wield it.

options.text: We shall project our power across the continent.

modifiers.name: Continental Ambition
modifiers.text: The highland empire looks outward. A professional army, hardened by campaigns on the African mainland, projects Malagasy power across the region, though the neglected navy pays the price.

options.text: We shall defend our sovereignty against all comers.

modifiers.name: Defiant Sovereignty
modifiers.text: Madagascar stands alone and inviolate. The realm's diplomatic skill and mercenary reserves ensure that no foreign power can threaten its independence.

destiny.name: Comoros Conquest
destiny.text: The Comoro Islands (Anjouan, Grand Comore, and Mayotte) are the natural stepping stones from Madagascar to the African coast. Seize them and establish Malagasy dominion over the northern Mozambique Channel.

conditions.text: Chose Island of a Thousand Ports
Own Nzwani, or a subject owns it
Own Ngazidja, or a subject owns it
Own Maore, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Fall of the Comoros
event.text:
The outrigger war fleets of Madagascar have swept across the Mozambique Channel. One by one, the sultanates of the Comoro Islands (Anjouan, Grand Comore, Mayotte) have fallen to Malagasy arms. The channel that separates Madagascar from Africa is now a Malagasy lake.

From these island outposts, the fleet can range further than ever before. The Swahili coast beckons.

options.text: The channel is ours. The coast will follow.

destiny.name: Swahili Reach
destiny.text: The great Swahili trading cities of Zanzibar and Kilwa have controlled Indian Ocean commerce for centuries. Take them, bring ivory into your markets, and make Madagascar the hub of East African trade.

conditions.text: Own Zanzibar, or a subject owns it
Own Kilwa, or a subject owns it
A market the country is in

children.text: Ivory is produced in the market
Ivory is traded in the market

event.title: Masters of the Swahili Coast
event.text:
Zanzibar and Kilwa (the ancient jewels of East African commerce) now fly the Malagasy banner. Ivory, gold, and enslaved captives flow through markets that Madagascar controls. The realm has become the dominant power of the western Indian Ocean.

The question is whether to entrench this trading empire through commercial institutions or to ride the monsoon winds to even greater reach.

modifiers.name: Swahili Trading Factories
modifiers.text: Permanent Malagasy trading factories on the Swahili coast serve as both commercial outposts and intelligence-gathering stations.

modifiers.name: Monsoon Trade Routes
modifiers.text: Mastery of the monsoon wind patterns allows Malagasy merchants to trade across the Indian Ocean with minimal overhead, reducing inflation and borrowing costs.

destiny.name: The Ocean Empire
destiny.text: From Mombasa to Mauritius, the Indian Ocean bows to Malagasy power. Command the trade routes, take Mombasa and Mauritius, and build an empire of a thousand ports that stretches from Africa to the open sea.

conditions.text: Own Mombasa, or a subject owns it
Own Mauritius, or a subject owns it

event.title: Ny Ranomasina Indianina
event.text:
The Indian Ocean (Ny Ranomasina Indianina in the Malagasy tongue) has become a Malagasy sea. From Mombasa on the African coast to Mauritius in the open ocean, Malagasy ships dominate the trade routes. The outrigger canoe that once carried a handful of Austronesian settlers to an uninhabited island has become the instrument of an empire.

The realm must decide how to govern this vast maritime domain.

options.text: Rule the seas as sultans of the southern ocean.

modifiers.name: Sultan of the Southern Seas
modifiers.text: The Malagasy state commands respect as the preeminent power of the southern Indian Ocean, backed by disciplined cavalry and artillery and a wide diplomatic network.

modifiers.name: Thousand-Port Empire
modifiers.text: A vast maritime empire held together not by a single army but by a network of ports, mercenaries, and vassal states that makes war cheap and resistance costly.

units.name: Lakana
units.text: The lakana is the traditional Malagasy outrigger canoe, descended directly from the vessels that carried the first Austronesian settlers across the Indian Ocean. Light, fast, and perfectly adapted to coastal waters.

units.name: Mpiambina Warriors
units.text: Highland spear warriors who form the backbone of Merina levies. Armed with iron-tipped spears and ox-hide shields, they fight with the ferocity of men defending their ancestral hills.

units.name: Sakalava Warband
units.text: Spearmen of the western plains with hide shields and no armour. They move fast through a country they know and strike first, and they pay for it when the fight turns into a slog.

units.name: Lakana Raider
units.text: A larger war canoe designed for cross-channel raiding expeditions. These outriggers carry thirty or more warriors and can outrun any European vessel in shallow coastal waters.

units.name: Fanompoana Levies
units.text: Free subjects called to arms as part of the labor owed to the state. Every able man is liable, so the ranks are full. They open with thrown spears and the fire of a few traded muskets, and they are thinking of their rice fields.

units.name: Tafika Regulars
units.text: The standing regiments of the Merina army, armed with a mix of traditional spears and traded muskets. Drilled and disciplined, they are the instrument of the state's authority.

units.name: Merina Musketeers
units.text: Soldiers trained in European musket drill by British military advisors under King Radama's modernization program. They fire in disciplined volleys and hold formation under fire.

buildings.name: Rice Terrace
buildings.text: Irrigated terraced rice paddies carved into the highland hillsides, fed by carefully maintained canal systems. The Betsileo perfected this technique into the most productive farming in the Indian Ocean.

where.text: The location's raw material is Rice

buildings.name: Zebu Kraal
buildings.text: The valan'omby is the cattle pen of a Malagasy village, a pit ringed with earth and stone where the zebu are kept and counted. Before planting the herd is driven through the flooded paddies to trample the mud. It stands only in cattle country, where a penned herd thrives and the pasture yields more.

where.text: The location's raw material is Livestock

buildings.name: Rova Citadel
buildings.text: A fortified hilltop palace complex of stone walls, timber halls, and sacred enclosures. The rova combines military strongpoint with the ruler's residence and spiritual center: its massive stone disc gates sealed each night against intruders.

buildings.name: Lamba Weaving House
buildings.text: A workshop dedicated to weaving the lamba: the distinctive Malagasy silk and cotton cloth. The finest lamba akotofahana, with their intricate geometric patterns, take months to complete on traditional looms.

buildings.name: Antemoro Paperworks
buildings.text: The scribes of the Matitanana valley boil and beat the bark of the avoha tree into a soft, strong paper and dry it in the sun. On it they write the Sorabe: astrology, medicine and the genealogies of kings.

buildings.name: Voanjo Colony
buildings.text: A settlement of soldier-farmers sent from the highlands to hold a conquered province. It can be planted only among a people the state has not accepted, and it is dissolved when they are.

buildings.name: Fokon'olona Assembly Hall
buildings.text: A gathering place for the fokon'olona: the village council of elders that governs local affairs through consensus. Here disputes are mediated, communal labor organized, and the fady observed.

buildings.name: Trano Gasy Estate
buildings.text: The trano gasy (the traditional Malagasy house of fired brick and timber, oriented along the cardinal directions according to cosmic principles) serves as the architectural expression of aristocratic status in the highlands.

buildings.name: Tsena Market
buildings.text: A bustling central marketplace where rice, cattle, cloth, and imported goods change hands. The tsena draws merchants from across the island and connects highland producers to coastal traders.

buildings.name: Musket Workshop
buildings.text: A specialized iron-working facility where skilled artisans, conscripted through fanompoana, repair imported muskets, manufacture spearheads, and forge the weapons that arm the realm's expanding military.

buildings.name: Sekoly School
buildings.text: An educational institution where missionaries and state teachers instruct students in reading, writing, and arithmetic, spreading literacy beyond the traditional Antemoro scholarly caste.

buildings.name: Rova Manjakamiadana
buildings.text: The Great Palace of Manjakamiadana ('Where It Is Pleasant to Rule') crowns the highest hill of Antananarivo. Built of stone and rosewood, it is the supreme symbol of Merina sovereignty: part ruler's residence, part administrative center, part sacred site where the hasina of the ancestors concentrates.

buildings.name: Lakana Arsenal
buildings.text: A great shipyard and naval arsenal where the largest war canoes of the Malagasy fleet are built and maintained. Rows of lakana stand in covered slipways, their hulls caulked with coconut fiber and their outriggers fitted with platforms for archers and musketeers.

list.name: Fokonolona
list.text: The fokonolona is the village council, foundational unit of Malagasy political life. Andrianampoinimerina formalised it during the reunification of Imerina (1787), seating elders and notables in open assembly to allocate communal labour, maintain irrigation canals, settle disputes through kabary oratory, and police local taboos. Royal decrees were read out in the assembly square; the king's word reached every village through the elders, not through appointed magistrates. Nineteenth-century French observers reckoned it the most genuinely participatory African institution they encountered.

list.name: Fanompoana
list.text: Fanompoana was the corvee labour owed personally to the sovereign in lieu of monetary tax. Modest under Andrianampoinimerina, it became permanent for ironworkers and apprenticed gunsmiths under Radama I (from 1820), and metastasised under Ranavalona I: fanompoana labourers fed the royal workshops with charcoal and iron, and the standing army was filled by conscription-as-fanompoana. The system gave the crown a body of state labour the silver treasury could never afford, and the villages of Imerina were thinned under the combined weight of corvee, conscription, and famine.

list.name: Andriana Caste Hierarchy
list.text: The Merina social order rested on three principal castes: Andriana nobles, Hova free commoners, and Andevo slaves, with the Andriana further divided into six endogamous sub-strata, each with inherited offices, marriage rules, and tomb-privilege. Hova managed rice-lands as owners and traders but could not rise to noble rank; Andevo were considered olona maloto (impure) and barred from owning land. Andrianampoinimerina codified the rules; Ranavalona I defended them against missionary egalitarianism. The caste system was the architecture of Merina political life.

list.name: Mpitahiry Sampy
list.text: The Mpitahiry Sampy were the keeper-lineages of the twelve great royal idols (Kelimalaza, Ramahavaly, Manjakatsiroa and others) consolidated by Andriamasinavalona's successors. Each sampy had its own oracular voice, sacrificial calendar, and keeper-priesthood; collectively they conferred hasina (sacred power) on the king and validated his decrees. Andrianampoinimerina sought their oracles before campaigns; Ranavalona I, after expelling the missionaries in 1835, made the cult of the royal sampy state policy and revived the Fandroana royal-bath ceremony in their presence.

list.name: Royal Workshops of Ilafy
list.text: In the early 1830s Jean Laborde, a French castaway and a blacksmith's son, set up a factory for Ranavalona I at Ilafy, north of Antananarivo, where muskets were made and gunpowder was mixed for the royal monopoly. It followed the workshops of Radama I, in which artisan missionaries had taught smithing, tanning, weaving and soap boiling since the 1820s. Fanompoana labourers carried in the charcoal and the iron. The workshops gave the kingdom arms it did not have to buy from Europeans, at the cost of the villages that fed and fuelled them.
